entries.why_wrong: This line just declares the `greet` function and its `name` parameter — nothing here formats or outputs a string, so there's no interpolation syntax to get wrong. The actual bug is in how the string literal builds its output, not in how the function or parameter is defined.

This line only returns whatever value `message` already holds — it doesn't build or format the string, so it can't be where an interpolation typo happens. The broken `{name}` placeholder was already baked into the string one line earlier, before this return ever runs.

This is just the closing brace ending the function body; it contains no string or expression at all. A missing `$` in template interpolation can only occur inside the template literal itself, not on a line that merely closes a block.
